metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VLC, navigated Tools > Preferences > All > Interface > Main interfaces > Qt, changed 'Maximum Volume displayed' from 125 to 200, and saved.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC advanced preferences tree and edit the qt-max-volume numeric field.
metadata.explanation: Same navigation path as the source trajectory but targets a different value (150 instead of 200). Evaluator reads /home/user/.config/vlc/vlcrc and checks qt-max-volume=150. Initial state (125) does not pass.
metadata.task_rationale: Diversity variation: same VLC preferences skill applied to a different numeric target value.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads /home/user/.config/vlc/vlcrc, the persistent storage for VLC Qt preferences, which is the right file for this setting.
The key 'qt-max-volume' is the correct VLC preference key for the maximum volume displayed in the Qt interface.
Getter correctly skips comment lines (VLC stores defaults as '#qt-max-volume=125', changed values as uncommented 'qt-max-volume=150'), so parsing logic is accurate.
Default value of '125' ensures the initial state (VLC unmodified) correctly fails the check, providing negative-control resistance.
Metric performs string comparison between result['qt_max_volume'] and str(expected_max_volume)='150', which is semantically correct since the file stores the value as a plain string.
No postconfig needed: verification reads a config file, not a transient UI/dialog state, so the check is stable.
Single instruction requirement (set max volume to 150) is fully covered by a single check — no missing sub-goals.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Use an exact key match (e.g., line.startswith('qt-max-volume=') or split on '=' and check key equality) instead of the substring check 'qt-max-volume=' in line, to avoid theoretical false matches on similarly named keys.
